System description:
# Case: Tesla Model S with Autopilot (Williston, Florida, 2016)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-17/02. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2015 Tesla Model S has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings and objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, slows down for a vehicle ahead in the same lane, and speeds up again when the lane is clear.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle centered in its lane using lane markings and the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: the system checks that the driver's hands are on the steering wheel by sensing steering torque, and shows visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users include cars, large trucks crossing or joining the road, and motorcyclists.

## Operating context
Autopilot is intended mainly for highways with limited access, in good visibility. Drivers can also turn it on for other roads, such as divided highways with cross traffic at intersections.

requirements.text: The system shall classify and track an object as a potential hazard whenever its predicted path intersects the vehicle's path within the system's sensor coverage, regardless of whether the object is classified as background or outside the travel lane; uncertain classifications shall not suppress hazard tracking.
TACC shall reduce speed when a detected vehicle is predicted to intersect the vehicle's path, even if that vehicle is not identified as being in the same lane.
While Autopilot is engaged, the system shall use driver-facing attention monitoring and issue an alert if the driver's gaze is directed away from the road for more than 2 seconds.
When the system predicts a collision with a detected vehicle, forward collision warning shall be issued no later than 4 seconds before predicted impact, when the vehicle is within sensor coverage.

Automatic emergency braking shall apply braking when a detected vehicle's predicted path intersects the vehicle's path and a collision is imminent, regardless of whether the vehicle is classified as being in the same lane.
The system shall not treat steering torque alone as evidence that the driver is holding the wheel; it shall alert if independent sensing does not confirm hand contact with the wheel.
The system shall inhibit Autopilot activation on roads with at-grade cross traffic.
TACC shall not resume the driver's set speed until the vehicle's projected path is clear of detected objects that could intersect it, including objects entering from outside the lane.
When a truck is detected crossing or joining the vehicle's path with insufficient clearance for safe passage, the system shall warn the driver and reduce speed or brake to avoid a collision.

The system shall detect a pedestrian entering or crossing the vehicle's path, including outside expected crossing locations, and warn the driver and apply automatic braking when needed to avoid a collision.
